editor.tooltip.sector.make_door: Turns this floor into a door: pressing Use (an Interact ray) on any wall of the sector, as an entity tagged Player, opens its ceiling to the lowest neighbouring ceiling minus the lip, waits, then closes it. Adds a new event tag "Door <sector name>", a Receive Ray event on every wall of the sector and a Door dispatch on the sector, all of which you can edit afterwards.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_teleporter: Turns this floor into a teleporter: an entity tagged Player that stands on it is sent to the centre of the destination sector's first floor, keeping its facing, with its velocity stopped. Click the button, then click the destination sector on the map. Adds a new event tag "Teleporter <sector name>", an Entity Grounded event and a Teleport Entities Inside dispatch on this sector, all of which you can edit afterwards. Something that just arrived by teleport isn't sent on again until it leaves the sector it landed in, so two teleporters can point at each other.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift: Turns this floor into a lift. Pick how it moves and what sets it off in the popup. Adds a new event tag "Lift <sector name>", the trigger events and a Lift (or Move To Height) dispatch on this sector, all of which you can edit afterwards. A switch elsewhere isn't made here: link one yourself with an event on the switch and the lift's tag.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.motion: How the floor moves. The first three use a Lift dispatch; the 'and Stay' ones a Move To Height, so the floor doesn't come back.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.motion.d: Goes down to its low height, waits, and comes back up to where it started.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.motion.u: Goes up to its high height, waits, and comes back down to where it started.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.motion.b: Starts going between its low and high heights, waiting at each, and never stops on its own. Triggers only start it; a Stop Movement you link yourself stops it.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.motion.d: Goes down to its low height and stays there.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.motion.u: Goes up to its high height and stays there.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.use_wall: Pressing Use (an Interact ray) on any wall of this sector, as an entity tagged Player, sets it off: a Receive Ray event on each wall.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.step_on: An entity tagged Player stepping onto this sector sets it off: an Entity Enter event, once per step, so a lowered lift still comes back while you stand on it.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.on_start: It sets itself off when the level starts: an On Start event. Mostly for Back and Forth.
editor.tooltip.sector.make_lift.once_onl: Each trigger event fires only once (Max Triggers 1): the walls once each, stepping on once, so it can still run once per kind of trigger.

Uses sharp nearest-neighbor filtering nearby with smoother mipmap transitions at a distance for a crunchy retro appearance.
Uses linear filtering and smooth mipmaps to create a soft, blurry low-resolution appearance similar to some Nintendo 64-era games.

editor.tooltip.wall.edit_sector: Open this wall's sector in the inspector.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture: Drag a texture from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture_middle: Fills the wall's openings, where both sides are open space - fences, bars, windows. Transparent pixels show through. Empty draws nothing. Only portal walls have openings.
editor.tooltip.wall.middle_has_collision: The middle blocks the player and rigidbodies.
editor.tooltip.wall.middle_ignored_by_ra: Raycasts pass through the middle: script raycasts, line of sight, and clicking it in the runtime editor.
editor.tooltip.wall.blocks_pathfinders: Pathfinders won't step across this wall, whatever the heights (Doom's block-monsters line). Everything else still can.
editor.tooltip.wall.blocks_sound: A Noise Alert crosses one of these walls and stops at the second (Doom's sound-block line). Only matters between two sectors.
editor.tooltip.wall.color: RGBA tint multiplied over the wall texture.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture_offset: UV offset for scrolling or aligning the wall texture.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture_scale: UV scale of the wall (makes the texture zoom in or out)
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.auto: Top edge, except the wall above a neighbour's ceiling, which uses its bottom edge. Doors and lifts carry their textures with them.
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.top_edge: The texture is pinned to the top edge and moves with it.
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.bottom_edge: The texture is pinned to the bottom edge and moves with it.
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.world: The texture is pinned to world height 0 and never moves. Use it for door tracks and to line up neighbouring walls.
editor.tooltip.texture.frame.duration: Seconds this frame shows before the next one.
editor.tooltip.texture.frame.duration_si: Only matters once the surface has two or more frames.
editor.tooltip.texture.frame.placement_t: Copies this frame's offset, scale, flips and offset per second onto every other frame. Textures and durations stay.
editor.tooltip.texture.frame.remove: Remove this frame. Removing the last one leaves the surface untextured.
editor.tooltip.texture.frame.add: Add a frame at the end. It starts as a copy of the last frame, placement included.
editor.tooltip.texture.animation.needs_f: Add a second frame to animate this surface.
editor.tooltip.texture.animation.loop: Plays the frames in order, then starts again from the first: 1 2 3 1 2 3.
editor.tooltip.texture.animation.ping_po: Plays the frames forward, then back: 1 2 3 2 1 2 3.
editor.tooltip.texture.animation.once: Plays the frames once, then stays on the last one. Starts again each Play, and when a script or dispatch changes the frames.
editor.tooltip.texture.offset_per_second: Map units this frame's texture moves every second (X, Y), on top of its offset. The scroll keeps going between frames; only its speed changes. Moves in Play and in the 3D view; the 2D view shows it still.
editor.tooltip.texture.frame.menu: Frame options: move, duplicate, copy its placement to the other frames, remove. Right-click the header too.
editor.tooltip.wall.delete: Remove this wall from the map.
editor.tooltip.entity.common.delete: Delete this entity from the level.
editor.tooltip.entity.snap_to_wall: Then right-click a wall to stick the entity to it. It can only slide along the wall and up or down, and always faces away from it.
editor.tooltip.entity.snap_to_wall_cance: Stop choosing a wall. Escape or right-clicking anything that isn't a wall does the same.
editor.tooltip.entity.disable_wall_snap: Let the entity move freely again. It stays where it is.
editor.tooltip.entity.switch_sides: Move the entity to the other side of its wall.
editor.tooltip.entity.wall_gap: How far off the wall the entity sits.
editor.tooltip.entity.snap_to_floor: Moves the entity down or up onto the floor it is in: the sector under it, and of that sector's floors the one nearest its height. Does nothing outside every sector.
editor.tooltip.component.decal.abs_heigh: When enabled, verticalPos is an absolute world height instead of a relative offset.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.so: Drag a sound (.wav, .mp3, .ogg or .flac) from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.re: Distance at which volume is at full gain.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ma: Beyond this distance sound is inaudible.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ro: How quickly the volume drops with distance.
editor.tooltip.component.script.file: Drag a .lua file from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.component.script.open_fil: Opens this script in the script editor.
editor.tooltip.component.player_controll: Milliseconds before landing where a jump input is buffered.
Vertical offset from entity origin to the camera eye.
Pressing this key casts a ray from the eye along the view. Click, then press a key; right click clears it.
How far the use ray reaches.
The ray's type. What it hits fires its Receive Ray events of this type. General fires nothing.
Whether this player controller is currently receiving input.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.fov: Vertical field of view in degrees.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.is_activ: Whether this camera is currently rendering.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.sphere: Sphere radius, multiplied by the Transform's Scale X.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.step_s: Max height, in world units, the collider can step up without being blocked. Not affected by the Transform's Scale.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.max_sl: Steepest floor, in degrees, the collider can stand on. On a steeper one it isn't grounded and slides down.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.capsul: Capsule radius: half its width. Multiplied by the Transform's Scale X.
Capsule height from bottom to top, rounded ends included. Multiplied by the Transform's Scale Y, and at least twice the radius.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.is_tri: Triggers detect overlap but do not physically block movement.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.mass: Mass in arbitrary units. Must be > 0 for dynamic bodies.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.gravi: Gravity multiplier (0 = floats, negative = repelled upward).
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.is_st: Static bodies are unmovable by physics but still collide.
editor.tooltip.component.model.file_name: Drag a model from the Asset Browser here. Its textures load automatically. The model is fitted to a unit box standing on the transform position, so Transform scale is its size in world units.
editor.tooltip.component.flipbook.file_n: Drag a .fpk flipbook from the Asset Browser here.
editor.tooltip.component.flipbook.sprite: Which of this entity's sprites the flipbook animates. The flipbook uses that sprite's side count.
editor.tooltip.component.flipbook.speed: Playback rate. 1 = the flipbook's own timing, 2 = twice as fast, 0 = frozen.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.inpu: Position walks to a fixed point. Entity follows another entity and keeps up as it moves.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.dest: The world point to walk to.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.targ: The entity to follow. Drag one here from the hierarchy or the map. If it is destroyed, the Pathfinder stops; while it is disabled, it heads for where the entity was last.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.offs: Added to the target's position on the world axes, e.g. Y 32 to aim above it.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.spee: World units per second. Slowed and paused by the time scale.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.air: Flies: ignores step height and drop-offs, and rises or sinks toward the destination's height, staying between the floor and ceiling.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.rang: Stops once the destination is within Range instead of walking right up to it.
How close, in world units, a ranged entity gets before it stops.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.keep: Keeps walking toward the destination once in Range, as Doom's monsters do. Off stops in Range.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.can_: Walks off ledges higher than its Step Size instead of refusing to. Falls by its Rigidbody.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.open: A closed door in the way gets opened: the sector's Door dispatch, with this entity as the instigator. Like Doom's monsters it never closes one, and not a locked one without the tag.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.faci: What it turns to face: where it walks, the destination, or nothing (scripts and dispatches decide).
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.turn: How it turns to where it walks: Doom's 45 degrees per chase step, or at once.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.chas: Seconds per chase step: how often it turns, and what the direction holds count. Doom: 3/35 (0.0857).
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.hold: Chase steps it keeps a direction at least, before choosing again. Doom: 1.
Chase steps it keeps a direction at most. Doom: 16. Lower looks more direct, higher wanders more.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.dead: This close on an axis counts as there when choosing a direction, and is its reach for arriving. Doom: 10.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.swap: Percent chance to try the shorter axis first, which helps it get unstuck. Doom: about 21.5.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.floa: Units per second it rises and sinks. Doom: 140.
It changes height once the height difference times this is more than the distance left. Doom: 3. 0 = always.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.push: With a Rigidbody, velocity from anything else (knockback) goes on top of the walking and keeps this share of its speed per 1/35 second. Doom: 0.90625. 0 = no pushes, 1 = never fades.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder.stuc: Seconds without progress before Pathfinder Stuck fires. 0 = never.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.targ: Who it hunts: entities with any of these tags. Empty: entities with the Player tag.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.sigh: How wide it sees, centred on where it faces. Doom: 180.
How far it sees. 0 = no limit, as in Doom.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.near: Within this it notices all around, behind it too. Doom: 64.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.look: Seconds between looks while idle. Doom: 10/35 (0.2857).
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.hear: Wakes on a Noise Alert that reaches its sector.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.ambu: A noise only wakes it with the target in sight (Doom's Ambush flag). It still notices what it sees.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.star: Chases from the first frame, nearest target first, without having to notice anyone.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.has_: Fires Melee Ready and OnMeleeReady with the target in reach. The attack itself is yours.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.mele: Melee reach, plus the target's collider radius. Doom: 44.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.has_: Fires Missile Ready and OnMissileReady on a roll that favours close targets. The attack itself is yours.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.reac: Seconds chasing before its first missile. Being hurt ends it early. Doom: 24/35 (0.686).
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.miss: No missile closer than this (the Revenant's 196). 0 = no limit.
No missile further than this (the Arch-Vile's 896). 0 = no limit.
Taken off the distance before the roll. Each unit left is 1 in 256 less chance. 128 more comes off without a melee attack. Doom: 64.
The distance is then multiplied by this: lower fires more (the Cyberdemon's 0.5). Doom: 1.
However far, at most this many of 256 rolls fail. Doom: 200.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.atta: Seconds it stands still after deciding to attack, Doom's attack animation. Make it match yours.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.chas: Seconds per decision while chasing. Doom: 3/35 (0.0857).
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.aggr: Fires while walking and without a gap between attacks (Doom's -fast).
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.face: Turns to the target when it decides to attack.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.pain: Percent chance a Hurt causes pain: Pain event, OnPain and the Pain Pause. Also makes its next missile certain. The Imp's: 78.4.
Seconds it stands still in pain.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.heal: It dies at 0: it stops thinking and walking, plays Dying, fires Died and OnDeath, and stays in the level as a corpse. A Hurt with damage takes this down.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.walk: Plays on this entity's first Flipbook while its Pathfinder walks, and holds on its frame while it stands still. Empty: left alone.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.atta: Plays from its start when it decides to attack, until Attack Pause ends. Empty: left alone.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.die_: Plays from its start when it dies. Make it a Once flipbook to end on the corpse frame. Empty: the flipbook just stops.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.infi: A Hurt turns it on its attacker, unless it was turned very recently. Wakes it if idle.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.targ: After turning on an attacker, seconds before another can turn it (Doom's threshold, 300/35 = 8.57).
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.acti: Percent chance per decision of the Active event and OnActive, Doom's active sound. Doom: about 1.17.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai.driv: Sends this entity's Pathfinder after the target, and holds it while idle. Off leaves it to you.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.fps: How fast frames change. A frame with its own duration ignores this.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.loop_mode: Once: stops on the last frame. Loop: starts over. Ping-pong: plays forward, then backward.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.play_on_s: Starts playing as soon as the level starts. Otherwise a script starts it with Play().
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.frame_row: Click to show it in the preview. Drag to reorder. Double-click to rename. Right-click for more.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.duration: How long this frame stays on screen, in seconds. 0 uses the flipbook's frames per second.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.event: A function in the entity's scripts called when playback reaches this frame, e.g. Footstep. It gets the frame's name. Leave empty for no event.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.smooth_s: When active, the camera will smoothly step up/down the sector instead of abruptly teleporting
editor.tooltip.sector.add_floor: Adds another room interval above the current highest floor.
editor.tooltip.sector.remove_floor: Removes this room interval. A sector must contain at least one floor.
editor.tooltip.sector.invalid_floor_heig: The floor intervals overlap or the ceiling is not above the floor.
editor.tooltip.sector.floor: One vertical room interval inside the sector, defined by a floor plane and a ceiling plane.
editor.tooltip.component.transform.heigh: Vertical distance above the current sector floor, rather than an absolute world position.
editor.tooltip.component.transform.floor: The sector floor interval that the entity belongs to.
editor.tooltip.component.sprite.directio: Controls how many viewing directions use separate sprite images. Single uses one image, 4-Sided uses 90-degree steps, and 8-Sided uses 45-degree steps.
editor.tooltip.component.sprite.is_stati: If true, the sprite stays still instead of facing towards the camera
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.pi: Playback-rate and pitch multiplier. 1.0 uses the sound's original pitch.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ga: Volume multiplier for this source. 1.0 uses the sound's original volume.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.co: Makes the sound directional based on the direction the audio source is facing.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ou: Volume multiplier used outside the outer sound cone. 0 = silent, 1 = unchanged.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.aspect_r: Ratio of viewport width to height, such as 16:9.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.type_b: Axis-aligned bounding box collider. Its faces remain aligned with the world axes.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.box_sc: Full size of the box collider along its X, Y, and Z axes, multiplied by the Transform's Scale.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.frict: Resistance to sliding while the body is in contact with another surface.
editor.tooltip.component.ui_transform.an: Normalized lower anchor inside the parent UI element. (0,0) is bottom-left and (1,1) is top-right.
Normalized upper anchor inside the parent UI element. Separating it from Min Anchor stretches the element.
editor.tooltip.component.ui_transform.pi: Normalized point inside the element used as the origin for positioning, rotation, and scaling.

editor.ui.sprite.title: Sprite
editor.tooltip.ui.sprite.draw_order: Higher draws on top of lower, across all UI, whichever UI layout each image is in. Equal numbers keep the layout order. Text is always on top of every image.
editor.tooltip.ui.sprite.color: Multiplied with the texture, RGBA 0..1. Alpha below 1 makes the image see-through. Without a texture the image is a solid rectangle of this colour, unless Fill When Empty is off.
editor.ui.button.title: Button
editor.tooltip.ui.button.interactable: Off: the button sends no events or callbacks and shows its Disabled look. It still blocks clicks to buttons under it.
editor.tooltip.ui.button.normal: Multiplied with the first Image's colour when nothing is happening, RGBA 0..1.
editor.tooltip.ui.button.hover: Multiplied with the first Image's colour while the cursor is over the button.
editor.tooltip.ui.button.pressed: Multiplied with the first Image's colour while the button is held down.
editor.tooltip.ui.button.disabled: Multiplied with the first Image's colour while Interactable is off.
editor.tooltip.ui.button.texture: Shown instead of the first Image's texture in this state. Empty: the Image's own texture.
editor.ui.button.no_sprite: Add an Image to see the button's states.
editor.ui.button.not_first: Only the entity's first Button works. This one does nothing.
editor.ui.sprite.no_texture: No texture: drawn as a solid rectangle of the colour below.

editor.tooltip.ui.sprite.native_size: Sizes the element to the texture's own size in pixels.
editor.tooltip.ui.sprite.native_size_str: Not available while the anchors stretch the element: its size comes from the anchors.
editor.ui.text.title: Text
editor.tooltip.ui.text.font_size: Text height in pixels at the project's UI Reference Height (Project Settings). It scales with the window's height.
editor.tooltip.ui.text.color: Text colour, RGBA 0..1. Alpha below 1 makes the text see-through.

editor.ui.transform.pivot_diagram_hint: Drag inside the box to set the pivot
editor.ui.transform.title: Transform

editor.ui.transform.tooltip_anchor_min: Top-left anchor point, as a fraction of the parent (0-1)
editor.ui.transform.tooltip_position: Offset from the anchor point, in pixels
editor.ui.transform.tooltip_resolved: Computed by the UI layout system - read only
editor.ui.transform.tooltip_rotation: Rotation in degrees, around the pivot
editor.ui.transform.tooltip_scale: Size in pixels. Ignored on an axis where the anchors are apart (stretched) - negative values flip the element
editor.ui.component.all_added: All available components are already on this entity

editor.ui.canvas.tooltip_frame: Fit the selection (or the whole screen) in the view. Shortcut: {key:ui_focus_selection}
editor.ui.canvas.tooltip_snap: Snap edges and centres to the screen's edges and centre while moving and resizing; also to the grid and the safe area while they're shown. Rotation snaps to 15 degrees. Hold {key:ui_disable_snap} to ignore it. Shortcut: {key:ui_toggle_snap}
editor.ui.canvas.tooltip_snap_elements: Also snap to the edges and centres of the other UI elements.

editor.ui.arrange.selected_count: %d selected - aligns to their combined bounds
editor.ui.arrange.to_screen: One selected - aligns to the screen
editor.ui.arrange.tooltip_distribute: Space the selected elements' centres evenly between the two outermost ones. Needs 3 or more.

editor.tooltip.grid.style: How the grid is drawn on the canvas: dots at each grid point, or whole lines. Snapping works the same in both.

editor.tooltip.grid.snap_to_grid: Snap new points to the grid.

editor.tooltip.staircase.calc_mode.targe: You choose the step length and the floor height the top step should reach; the step height is worked out automatically so the last step lands exactly on that target.
editor.tooltip.staircase.calc_mode.step_: You choose exactly how many steps and how tall each one is; the length of one step is worked out by dividing the rectangle evenly.
editor.tooltip.staircase.step_height: Height gained per step. Can be negative to build stairs going down.
editor.tooltip.staircase.step_length: Length of one step along the direction the staircase is drawn. The last step is shortened to fit the rectangle instead of overshooting it.
editor.tooltip.staircase.target_floor_he: Floor height the final step should reach. Can be below the starting floor height to build stairs going down.
editor.tooltip.staircase.step_count: Exact number of steps to generate. Must be at least 1.
