editor.geometry.title: Wall Editing
editor.tooltip.geometry.drag_carries_ent: When dragging walls moves a whole sector, the entities standing in it move along. Entities snapped to a wall stay on it.
editor.geometry.hint.select: Click a wall to select it and open its inspector. Click empty space to deselect.
editor.geometry.hint.drag: Drag a wall to move it, or drag a square handle to move that endpoint. Connected walls follow shared corners.
editor.geometry.hint.delete: {key:multi_select}/{key:range_select} click to multi-select ({key:multi_select}+right click works too). {key:delete} removes the selected walls.
editor.entity_mode.title: Entity Editing
editor.entity_mode.hint.create: Press {key:place_entity} to place the palette's selection under the cursor.
editor.entity_mode.hint.edit: Right click an entity to open its inspector. {key:multi_select}+right click to edit several together.
editor.entity_mode.hint.move: Drag an entity with the left mouse button to move it. Dragging one entity in a selection moves all of them.
editor.entity_mode.hint.gizmo: Drag the red or blue arrow to move along X or Z, or the green square to move freely. Both snap to the grid; hold {key:disable_snap} to ignore it.
editor.entity_mode.hint.select: {key:multi_select}/{key:range_select} click to multi-select. Click empty space to deselect. {key:delete} removes the selected entities.
editor.entity_mode.hint.copy: {key:copy_entities} copies the selected entities, {key:paste_entities} pastes them at the cursor.
editor.entity_mode.hint.focus: Press {key:focus_selection} to center the view on the selection.
editor.tooltip.filters: Untick to hide this kind from picking. Hidden ones are drawn faintly and can't be clicked or dragged. Resets when the editor restarts.
editor.tooltip.geometry.split: Splits each selected wall in half. {key:split_wall}+click a wall to split it at the cursor instead.
editor.geometry.split_nothing: Nothing to split: the walls are too short.
editor.geometry.split_too_close: Too close to the end of the wall to split there.
editor.tooltip.geometry.merge: Joins selected walls that continue each other in a straight line, with the same sectors on each side and no other wall at the shared corner. The first wall's properties are kept.
editor.geometry.merge_nothing: Nothing to merge: the selected walls don't continue each other.
editor.tooltip.geometry.batch: Writes the ticked values to every selected wall. Unticked values are left alone.
editor.tooltip.geometry.align.chain: Starts at the wall you clicked last and follows the connected selected walls, so the texture continues across each corner. Walls running the other way get Flip X. Vertical offsets are copied from the first wall.
editor.geometry.align.chain_nothing: No selected wall connects to the first one.
editor.tooltip.geometry.align.reset: Sets the top and bottom texture offsets of the selected walls to 0.
editor.tooltip.geometry.align.fit: Sets the vertical texture scale so the texture fits the tallest visible part of the wall exactly once, and the vertical offset to 0. Horizontal scale is unchanged.
editor.geometry.align.fit_nothing: None of the selected walls has a visible part to fit.
editor.geometry.hint.split: {key:split_wall}+click a wall to split it at the cursor (snaps to the grid; hold {key:disable_snap} to ignore it).
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.palette.refre: Looks for .prefab files under Assets again.
runtime_editor.tooltip.palette: What {key:rt_place_entity} places: an empty entity or a prefab. Shared with the map editor's Entity Mode palette.
runtime_editor.palette.hint: Pick what to place, then press {key:rt_place_entity} while pointing at a surface or an entity.
editor.entity_mode.palette.hint: Pick what to place, then press {key:place_entity} over the canvas. Prefabs can also be dragged onto the canvas.
editor.entity_mode.palette.place_failed: Could not place the selected prefab. Check the logs.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.placement.on_: New entities stand on the floor of the sector under the cursor. Off, they are placed at height 0.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.placement.ran: Turns each new entity to a random direction around the vertical axis.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.placement.tag: A project tag every new entity gets. Leave empty for none.
editor.entity_mode.placement.tag_unknown: No project tag has this name; add it under Project Settings > Tags.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.align: Lines the selection up on the lowest, middle or highest value of the selection on that axis.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.distribute: Spaces the selection evenly between its two outermost entities on that axis. Needs 3 or more.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.snap: Moves each selected entity to the nearest grid point. Height is kept.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.drop: Puts each selected entity on the floor of the sector it is in.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.make_prefab: Saves each selected entity as its own .prefab in Assets/Prefabs, named after the entity, and links the entity to it.
editor.entity_mode.make_prefab_failed: Could not create the prefab. Check the logs.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.filter.select: Selects every entity of this kind.
editor.project.event_tags_hint: Link events to dispatches. Only these can be picked as an event's or dispatch's tag.
editor.tooltip.project.ui_reference_heig: Window height that UI Text Font Sizes are given at. Text is drawn at Font Size x window height / this.
editor.project.ui_reference_height_faile: Could not save the UI Reference Height to project.tilky. Check the logs.
editor.project.clear_saves_confirm:
Delete every save file this project made while playing in the editor?
This can't be undone.
editor.tooltip.project.clear_saves: Deletes everything scripts saved with Saving while you played in the editor (the project's Saves folder), so the next Play starts fresh. Players' saves from an exported game aren't touched.
editor.tooltip.project.texels_per_unit: Texture pixels per world unit at texture scale 1. A texture covers its pixel size / this, so it keeps its shape. At 4, a 128px wall texture is 32 units tall.
editor.project.texels_per_unit_failed: Could not save Texels Per Unit to project.tilky. Check the logs.
tags.none_available: No more tags. Create them in Project Settings.
tags.tooltip.delete: Delete this tag from the project. Removes it from every sector, wall and entity that has it.
tags.notification.duplicate_name: A tag with that name already exists.
tags.notification.save_failed: Failed to save project settings. Check logs.
editor.tooltip.tag_delete: Remove this tag from here. The tag itself is not deleted from the project.
editor.tooltip.sector.add_script: Attach a Lua script to this sector. The script gets a `sector` global that refers to this sector.
editor.tooltip.sector.remove_script: Detach this script from the sector.
editor.tooltip.sector.parent: Drag a sector here from the hierarchy, or pick one from the list. When the parent's values change, this sector's values change by the same amount.
sector.parent_cycle_error: Can't use this sector as the parent: it is this sector or one of its children.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.ui_design: How the editor's panels and menus look. Press Save to keep it for next time.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.texture_fie: Size in pixels of the texture previews in the wall and sector inspectors.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.runtime_cam: Field of view of the runtime editor's camera, in degrees. Only affects the editor view, not the game's cameras.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.remember_ca: On: the runtime editor opens where its camera was last left. Off: it opens at the mouse's position in the 2D view, at eye height above the floor there.
events.title: Events
dispatches.title: Dispatches
Walk to a sector's centre, on one of its floors.
Follow an entity, keeping up as it moves.
Follow whoever set off the event (e.g. whoever shot it, for a Receive Ray event). Skipped when the event has no instigator.
Hold still for some seconds, keeping any push and a flyer's height, then carry on. Good for pain or an attack.
Choose a direction again now, instead of finishing the current one.
Chase the player: the first enabled entity with the Player tag.
Chase whoever set off the event. Skipped when the event has no instigator.
Takes Damage off its health, the instigator as the attacker. At 0 it dies. Otherwise it rolls Pain Chance and may turn on them.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.monster_ai_act: What to do with this entity's Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.monster_ai_dam: Taken off its health. 0 only rolls pain.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.noise_target: Who the monsters that hear it go after.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.pathfinder_act: What to do with this entity's Pathfinder. Going somewhere doesn't tick a stopped Pathfinder: add a Resume too.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.pathfinder_use: Fill Position from this entity's current position.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.pathfinder_sec: The sector whose centre to walk to. Drag one here from the map.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.pathfinder_ent: The entity to follow. Drag one here from the hierarchy or the map.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.pathfinder_off: Added to the followed entity's position, on the world axes.
editor.tooltip.events.link_tag: An event runs every dispatch with the same tag, on any wall, sector or entity.
editor.tooltip.events.max_triggers: How many times this event can fire during play. 0 = no limit.
editor.tooltip.events.chance: Chance to fire each time it happens. A failed roll doesn't count toward Max Triggers.
editor.tooltip.events.filter: Which entities can set this event off, by their tags. Include: entities with any of the filter tags. Exclude: entities with none of them. All: every entity.
editor.tooltip.events.filter_tags: The tags the filter checks. An entity only needs one of them.
editor.tooltip.events.filter_tag_remove: Remove this tag from the filter.
editor.tooltip.events.direction: Forward = from the wall's front side to its back side.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.color_speed: Color units (0-1) per second, per channel. 0 = instant.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.gap: How far short of the opposite surface the move stops.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.collision: What the move does when an entity is in the way.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.use_entity: Fill Position (Coordinates) and Rotation (Set) from this entity's current transform.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_to: Coordinates: exactly the Position below. Entity: where the target entity is, standing on the floor under it. Sector: the centre of the sector, standing on the floor picked below. Standing means grounded at once, with no fall.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_entit: The entity to teleport to. Pick it here or drag it in from the hierarchy or the map. If it's deleted, the teleport is skipped.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_secto: The sector to teleport to: its centre. Pick it here or drag it in from the map. If it's deleted, the teleport is skipped.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_floor: Which of the sector's floors to stand on, from the bottom.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_facin: Set: turns to the Rotation below. Keep Current: faces the same way as before. Use Target's: faces the way the target entity faces.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_stop_: Stops the entity's Rigidbody, so it doesn't slide or keep falling after the teleport. Off keeps its velocity.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.teleport_insid: Which of this sector's floors the entities have to stand on to be teleported, or any of them. Disabled entities are never teleported. They keep their spacing: each lands as far from the target point as it stood from this sector's centre.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.function_name: Called on every enabled script of this entity, with the entity that caused the event (or nil).
editor.tooltip.user_settings.event_link_: Width in pixels of the lines from the selected object's events to their dispatches.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.linedef_thi: Width in pixels of the line drawn for each linedef.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.linedef_end: Width and height in pixels of the square at each end of a linedef (3 = a 3x3 square).
linedef.title: Linedef
linedef.name: Name
editor.tooltip.linedef.enabled: A disabled linedef fires no events and typed rays pass through it. Dispatches can turn it on and off.
editor.tooltip.linedef.blocks_pathfinder: While enabled, Pathfinders won't step across it (Doom's block-monsters line). Everything else still can.
editor.tooltip.linedef.delete: Remove this linedef from the map.
editor.tooltip.linedef.mode: Draw and edit linedefs instead of walls: lines that carry events but are never drawn, never collide and never split sectors. {key:geometry_mode} toggles it while in Geometry Mode.
editor.linedef.title: Linedef Editing
editor.tooltip.linedef.split: Splits each selected linedef in half. {key:split_wall}+click a linedef to split it at the cursor instead.
editor.linedef.split_nothing: Nothing to split: the linedefs are too short.
editor.linedef.hint.draw: Click empty space, or the end of an unselected linedef, to start a linedef; click again to end it. Right click or Escape cancels.
editor.linedef.hint.select: Click a linedef to select it, right click to open its inspector. Drag on empty space to box-select.
editor.linedef.hint.drag: Drag a linedef to move it, or drag a square handle to move that end. Nothing else moves with it.
editor.linedef.hint.split: {key:split_wall}+click a linedef to split it at the cursor (snaps to the grid; hold {key:disable_snap} to ignore it).
editor.linedef.hint.delete: {key:multi_select}/{key:range_select} click to multi-select ({key:multi_select}+right click works too). {key:delete} removes the selected linedefs.
editor.key.add_comment: Add Comment (on what's under the cursor, or a pin)
editor.tooltip.linedef.flip: Swaps the start and end of each selected linedef, turning its front around. The tick marks the front: an entity crossing from that side crosses Forward. Shortcut: {key:flip_linedef}
editor.linedef.hint.flip: The tick in the middle of a linedef marks its front: crossing from that side is Forward. {key:flip_linedef} flips the selected linedefs.
editor.tooltip.events.condition: Only fire when this comparison is true. None = always. A failed condition doesn't count toward Max Triggers.
editor.tooltip.events.condition_to_varia: Compare against another variable instead of a number.
editor.tooltip.events.condition_to_numbe: Compare against a number instead of a variable.
events.variable.none_available: No variables. Add them in World Settings or Project Settings.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.variable: The level or global variable to change.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.operation: Set replaces the variable's value; Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide change it by Value. Dividing by 0 leaves it as it is.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.delay: Seconds between the event firing and this running. Each trigger queues its own run.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.cooldown: Seconds after it is called during which further calls do nothing. 0 = no cooldown.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.cooldown_trigg: How many calls it takes to start the cooldown. 1 starts it on every call.
editor.tooltip.events.collide_side: Which side of the line the entity's centre is on when it touches. A wall's front is its front sector's side; a linedef's is the side its tick points to.
editor.tooltip.events.stay_interval: Fires every this many seconds for each entity inside, counted from when it entered.
editor.tooltip.events.move_end: Reaching its target, being stopped (blocked with Stop, or by a Stop Movement), or arriving back after retracting.
editor.tooltip.events.ray_type: Only rays of this type fire it: the Player Controller's use key, or Game.Raycast / Camera:Raycast with a RayType.
editor.tooltip.events.first_hit_only: Fire only on the first hit of a run, again once a frame passes without that caster's ray hitting. Off fires on every hit.
editor.tooltip.events.ray_side: The side of the line the ray came from.
editor.tooltip.events.timer_interval: Fires every this many seconds while the game runs. Paused while its entity or linedef is disabled.
editor.tooltip.events.key_input: What fires it: a keyboard key or a mouse button. Key Press fires the frame it goes down, Key Release the frame it comes back up. It fires while the game is paused too, and never on a disabled entity or linedef. There is no instigator.
editor.tooltip.events.key: Click, then press the key. Escape cancels, right click clears it. With no key it never fires.
editor.tooltip.event.line.entity_collide: An entity's collider touches this wall or linedef. Side picks which side of the line it has to be on. The entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.line.entity_cross: An entity's centre crosses this wall or linedef, in the direction picked (Forward = from the front side to the back side). The entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.sector.entity_enter: An entity comes into this sector (arriving by teleport counts). Entities already inside when the level starts don't. The entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.sector.entity_exit: An entity leaves this sector. The entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.sector.entity_stay: Every Interval seconds for each entity inside this sector, each on its own clock from when it came in. The entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.sector.entity_groun: Every frame, for each entity whose Rigidbody stands on the ground in this sector. The entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.sector.move_finishe: A floor or ceiling move of this sector ends: reaching its target, being stopped, or arriving back after retracting. Surface, Floor and End narrow it down. No instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.entity.collide: This entity's collider touches another entity's. The filter checks the other entity's tags, and that entity is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.entity.change_secto: This entity moves from one sector into another. The filter checks the new sector's tags.
editor.tooltip.event.entity.grounded_in_: Every frame this entity's Rigidbody stands on the ground in a sector. The filter checks that sector's tags.
editor.tooltip.event.entity.enable: This entity is enabled again, by a dispatch, a script or the inspector.
editor.tooltip.event.entity.disable: This entity is disabled, by a dispatch, a script or the inspector.
editor.tooltip.event.entity.destroyed: This entity is about to be destroyed, whatever destroyed it. Not when the level unloads or play stops.
editor.tooltip.event.receive_ray: A typed ray hits this object: the Player Controller's use key (Interact), or Game.Raycast / Camera:Raycast with a ray type. The entity that cast it is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.condition_met: The event's own Condition goes from false to true. No instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.timer: Every Interval seconds, the first time after First Delay, counted from play start. Paused while its entity or linedef is disabled. No instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.lua_signal: A script calls Game.Signal with this event's Signal Name. The instigator is the entity the script passed, if any.
editor.tooltip.event.ui_button.click: The left mouse button goes down on this UI Button. The player is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.ui_button.release: The left mouse button is let go after a click on this UI Button, wherever the cursor is by then. The player is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.ui_button.hover_ent: The cursor comes onto this UI Button (the topmost one under it). The player is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.ui_button.hover_exi: The cursor leaves this UI Button, or another button comes on top of it there. The player is the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.pathfinder_arrived: This entity's Pathfinder gets to its destination (within Range when ranged), once per arrival. Following an entity, that entity is the instigator; walking to a point there is none. Only on an entity with a Pathfinder.
editor.tooltip.event.pathfinder_blocked: The way this entity's Pathfinder is walking gets blocked, at most once per chase step. No instigator. Only on an entity with a Pathfinder.
editor.tooltip.event.pathfinder_stuck: This entity's Pathfinder has made no progress for its Stuck Time. No instigator. Only on an entity with a Pathfinder.
editor.tooltip.event.pathfinder_started_: This entity's Pathfinder starts walking: where a walk animation goes. No instigator. Only on an entity with a Pathfinder.
editor.tooltip.event.pathfinder_stopped_: This entity's Pathfinder stops walking, for any reason: where an idle animation goes. No instigator. Only on an entity with a Pathfinder.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.target_spot: This entity's Monster AI wakes and starts chasing, by sight, sound or a dispatch: Doom's see sound. The target is the instigator. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.target_lost: This entity's Monster AI goes back to idle, having nothing left to chase. No instigator. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.melee_ready: This entity's Monster AI decides on a melee attack. Do the attack from here: the AI does none itself. The target is the instigator. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.missile_rea: This entity's Monster AI decides on a ranged attack. Do the attack from here: the AI does none itself. The target is the instigator. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.died: Its health reached 0. The attacker is the instigator, if there is one. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.pain: A Hurt passes this entity's Pain Chance roll. The attacker is the instigator, if there is one. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.monster.active: Now and then while chasing: Doom's active sound. See Active Chance. The target is the instigator. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.level.start: Once, when the level starts (after the scripts' Start), like a script's Start(). On an entity spawned later, once after it spawns. Never on a disabled entity or linedef. No instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.key.press: A key or mouse button goes down. Fires while the game is paused too, never on a disabled entity or linedef. No instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.key.release: A key or mouse button comes back up. Fires while the game is paused too, never on a disabled entity or linedef. No instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.line.set_c: Changes this wall's colour, sliding at Speed (0 = at once).
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.line.set_t: Changes the texture of one piece of this wall: top, middle or bottom. Empty removes it (an empty middle is an opening).
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.line.set_c: Turns on or off whether this wall's middle blocks movement.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.linedef.se: Turns this linedef on or off. A disabled linedef fires no events and rays pass it by.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.mov: Raises a floor of this sector up to its ceiling (less Gap), at Speed.
Lowers a ceiling of this sector down to its floor (plus Gap), at Speed.
Moves this sector's floor or ceiling to a height: a set height, an offset from where it is, or a neighbouring sector's height.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.doo: Opens and closes this sector's ceiling (with Split, its floor too): open, wait, close, or another Door Type. Can be locked to instigators with a tag.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.sto: Stops this sector's floor or ceiling where it is, ending a move, door, lift or stairs on it.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.lif: Moves this sector's floor down (or up), waits and brings it back, or keeps it going between two heights (Perpetual). Can be locked to instigators with a tag.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.rai: Doom-style stairs: this sector's floor rises one step, then each next sector with the same floor texture rises one step above the last.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.lig: Keeps this sector's light changing (flicker, strobe, glow or fire) until a None effect or a Set Light.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.set: Changes this sector's light, sliding at Speed (0 = at once). Stops a light effect.
Changes the texture of a floor or ceiling of this sector.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.change_tag: Adds one of the project's tags to this object, or removes it.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.tel: Moves this entity at once: to coordinates, to another entity or to a sector's centre, landing on the floor.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.sector.tel: Teleports the entities standing in this sector (picked by tag and floor) to coordinates, an entity or another sector, keeping their spacing.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.dis: Disables this entity: it stops moving, running scripts and firing events until it's enabled again.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.cal: Calls the function with this name in this entity's scripts, passing the instigator.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.cha: Adds to or replaces this entity's Rigidbody velocity, e.g. for a jump pad or a knockback.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.mov: Glides this entity to a position (or by an offset) at a speed or over a set time, optionally turning it too.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.set: Turns this entity's components of one type on or off, or toggles them.
Changes one field of one of this entity's components or scripts: set, add, multiply or toggle it, at once or over time.
Replaces the 8 directional textures of this entity's first Sprite.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.pat: Tells this entity's Pathfinder where to go: a point, a sector's centre, an entity or the instigator to follow. Or stops or resumes it. Only on an entity with a Pathfinder.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.mon: Wakes this entity's Monster AI on a target, puts it to sleep, or tells it it was hurt. Only on an entity with a Monster AI.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.noise_aler: Spreads a noise from here, through open doors and past at most one Blocks Sound wall. Sleeping Monster AIs it reaches wake on the target.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.spawn_pref: Spawns a prefab at this object (or at a world position), with an offset and a rotation.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.play_sound: Plays a sound from this object's position. The level's own plays without a position.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.show_messa: Shows a line of text on screen for a few seconds, in the style set in World Settings.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.relay: Runs other dispatches: every one on an event tag, or the named dispatches of one target. The instigator is passed on.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.reset_even: Sets the trigger count of every event on an event tag back to 0, so events with Max Triggers can fire again.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.load_level: Switches to another level at the end of the frame.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.pause: Pauses the game: game time stops and the cursor is unlocked and shown.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.resume: Resumes a paused game: game time runs again and the cursor goes back to the level's settings.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.quit: Closes the exported game at the end of the frame. In the editor, Play stops.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.entity.set: Replaces the text of this entity's first UI Text, or the prefix or suffix around the variable it shows.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.music: Plays, stops, pauses or switches the level's music, or sets its volume.
editor.tooltip.event.dispatch.change_var: Changes an event variable: set, add, subtract, multiply or divide it.
editor.tooltip.events.flow.condition.var: Calls the next dispatch only when an event-variable comparison holds.
editor.tooltip.events.flow.condition.cha: Calls the next dispatch with a random chance, rolled each time.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.self: The dispatches with this name on this object itself.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.instig: The dispatches with this name on the entity that set the event off. Only known while playing; an entity without one ignores the call.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.entity: The dispatches with this name on one entity you pick.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.sector: The dispatches with this name on one sector you pick.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.wall: The dispatches with this name on one wall you pick.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.linede: The dispatches with this name on one linedef you pick.
editor.tooltip.events.call_target.tagged: The dispatches with this name on everything with a tag: entities, sectors and walls.
editor.tooltip.event.payload.tag_type.in: Only things with at least one of the tags below.
editor.tooltip.event.payload.tag_type.ex: Only things with none of the tags below.
editor.tooltip.events.direction.forward: Only crossing from the line's front side to its back side.
editor.tooltip.events.direction.backward: Only crossing from the line's back side to its front side.
editor.tooltip.events.side.front: Only the front side: a wall's front sector side, or the side a linedef's tick points to.
editor.tooltip.events.side.back: Only the back side: away from a wall's front sector, or opposite a linedef's tick.
editor.tooltip.events.collision.force_mo: Moves through entities as if they weren't there.
editor.tooltip.events.collision.stop: Stops at the last height that fit.
editor.tooltip.events.collision.retract: Goes back to the height it started from.
editor.tooltip.events.collision.dont_mov: Holds still while blocked and carries on once it's clear.
editor.tooltip.event.condition.equal: Only when the variable equals the value.
editor.tooltip.event.condition.less_than: Only when the variable is less than the value.
editor.tooltip.event.condition.greater_t: Only when the variable is greater than the value.
editor.tooltip.event.condition.less_than: Only when the variable is less than or equal to the value.
editor.tooltip.event.condition.greater_t: Only when the variable is greater than or equal to the value.
editor.tooltip.events.operation.set: Replaces the value with the one given.
editor.tooltip.events.operation.add: Adds the value (to each channel of a vector or colour).
editor.tooltip.events.operation.multiply: Multiplies by the value (each channel of a vector or colour).
editor.tooltip.events.operation.divide: Divides by the value. Dividing by 0 leaves it as it is.
editor.tooltip.events.teleport.to.entity: Where another entity is, standing on the floor under it.
editor.tooltip.events.teleport.to.sector: The centre of a sector, standing on the floor picked.
editor.tooltip.events.teleport.facing.ke: Faces the same way as before the teleport.
editor.tooltip.events.teleport.facing.ta: Faces the way the target entity faces.
editor.tooltip.events.key_input.mouse_mi: The middle mouse button (pressing the wheel).
editor.tooltip.events.ray_type.general: Fires no events. For rays that only scripts look at.
editor.tooltip.events.ray_type.interact: Use rays: what the Player Controller's use key casts.
editor.tooltip.events.ray_type.line_of_s: Rays that check whether something can see something.
editor.tooltip.events.ray_type.custom: Your own kind of ray, cast by scripts.
editor.tooltip.events.surface.both: Both the floor and the ceiling.
editor.tooltip.events.surface.either: The floor or the ceiling, either one.
editor.tooltip.events.move_end.reached: The move got to its target.
editor.tooltip.events.move_end.stopped: It was stopped early: blocked with Stop, or by a Stop Movement.
editor.tooltip.events.move_end.retracted: It arrived back after retracting from an entity in the way.
editor.tooltip.events.toggle.toggle: Flips it: on becomes off and off becomes on.
editor.tooltip.events.wall_piece.top: The upper piece, above the opening into the next sector.
editor.tooltip.events.wall_piece.middle: The middle piece: the wall itself, or what fills the opening between two sectors.
editor.tooltip.events.wall_piece.bottom: The lower piece, below the opening (the face of a step).
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.absolu: The Height below, as a world height.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.relati: Where the surface is now, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.lowest: The lowest floor of the sectors next to this one, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.highes: The highest floor of the sectors next to this one, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.lowest: The lowest ceiling of the sectors next to this one, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.highes: The highest ceiling of the sectors next to this one, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.next_h: The closest neighbouring floor above where the surface is now, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.next_l: The closest neighbouring floor below where the surface is now, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.next_h: The closest neighbouring ceiling above where the surface is now, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.height_mode.next_l: The closest neighbouring ceiling below where the surface is now, plus Offset.
editor.tooltip.events.lift.type.down_wai: Goes down to its low height, waits, and comes back to where it started.
editor.tooltip.events.lift.type.up_wait_: Goes up to its high height, waits, and comes back to where it started.
editor.tooltip.events.lift.type.perpetua: Keeps going between its low and high heights, waiting at each, until a Stop Movement.
editor.tooltip.events.lift.low_mode.lowe: The lowest neighbouring floor, plus Lip.
editor.tooltip.events.lift.high_mode.hig: The highest neighbouring floor, plus Lip.
editor.tooltip.events.lift.retrigger.res: Heading back, it turns round; waiting, the wait starts over.
editor.tooltip.events.door.type.open_wai: Opens from where it is, waits, then closes.
editor.tooltip.events.door.type.close_wa: Closes an open door, waits, then reopens it to where it was. A shut door stays shut.
editor.tooltip.events.door.type.close_st: Closes an open door and leaves it shut.
editor.tooltip.events.door.type.toggle: Opens a shut door and closes an open one. Every run reverses it, even mid-move.
editor.tooltip.events.door.open_mode.low: Opens to the lowest neighbouring ceiling, minus Lip.
editor.tooltip.events.door.floor_open_mo: The floor goes down to the lowest neighbouring floor, plus Lip.
editor.tooltip.events.door.retrigger.res: Closing, it opens again; open, the wait starts over.
Opening, it closes again; shut, the wait starts over.
editor.tooltip.events.door.retrigger.tog: Every run reverses it, even mid-move.
editor.tooltip.events.door.retrigger.ign: Running it again while it's busy does nothing.
Random bright and dim stretches, up to the times set.
Slides down to dim and back up, at Speed.
Every Interval, a random step between bright and dim.
Stops the effect and puts the sector's own light back.
editor.tooltip.events.light_effect.dim_m: Dims to the light of the darkest neighbouring sector when the effect starts.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source: A sound that plays from the entity.
editor.tooltip.component.script: One of the entity's scripts: its public fields.
editor.tooltip.component.player_controll: Player movement, mouse look and the use key.
editor.tooltip.component.camera: A view the game can be seen through.
editor.tooltip.component.collider: The shape that collides and sets off contact events.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody: Velocity, gravity and standing on floors.
editor.tooltip.component.pathfinder: Walks the entity to a point or another entity, Doom style: 8 directions, stepping around what blocks it.
editor.tooltip.component.monster_ai: A Doom monster's brain: notices targets by sight and sound, decides when to attack and who to fight. It never attacks: its events and callbacks are where the attack goes.
editor.tooltip.component.ui_transform: Where a UI element sits on screen, and its size.
editor.tooltip.events.value_source.varia: An event variable's value at the moment it runs.
editor.tooltip.events.tag_operation.remo: Takes the tag away from this object.
editor.tooltip.events.velocity_mode.add: Adds to the current velocity, like a push.
editor.tooltip.events.move_timing.speed: Moves at a set speed, in units per second.
editor.tooltip.events.move_timing.durati: Takes a set number of seconds, however far it is.
editor.tooltip.events.ui_text_part.text: The UI Text's own text, shown when it shows no variable.
editor.tooltip.events.ui_text_part.prefi: The words before the variable it shows.
editor.tooltip.events.ui_text_part.suffi: The words after the variable it shows.
editor.tooltip.events.music.action.play: Resumes a paused track, or starts the list from the first track.
editor.tooltip.events.music.action.pause: Pauses the music where it is; Play resumes it.
editor.tooltip.events.music.action.switc: Plays one of the level's tracks now; the list carries on from there.
editor.tooltip.events.relay_mode.tag: Runs every dispatch listening on an event tag.
editor.tooltip.events.relay_mode.direct: Runs the named dispatches of one target, like an event's direct call.
editor.tooltip.events.first_delay: Seconds before the first time it fires.
editor.tooltip.events.signal_name: Game.Signal(name) from a Lua script fires every Lua Signal event with this name.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.line_texture: The new texture. It replaces every animation frame with this one, placed like the old first frame; the animation mode stays. Empty removes it; an empty middle is an opening.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.line_collision: Whether the wall's middle blocks movement.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.linedef_enable: A disabled linedef fires no events and typed rays pass through it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.height_mode: Where the surface goes. Neighbours are the sectors across this sector's two-sided walls; Offset is added to their height.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_lip: How far below the lowest neighbouring ceiling the door stops.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_wait: Seconds the door waits before heading back: open for Open, Wait, Close, shut for Close, Wait, Open.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_open_soun: Played from the sector when the door starts opening, including when it reopens while closing. Empty: no sound.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_close_sou: Played from the sector when the door starts closing. Empty: no sound.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_collision: What closing does when an entity is in the way. Retract reopens it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_retrigger: What happens when it runs again while the door is open or moving.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_type: Open, Wait, Close / Open and Stay: open from where the door is. Close, Wait, Open / Close and Stay: close an open door down to its floor and reopen it to where it was; a shut door stays shut. Toggle: opens a shut door, closes an open one, and every run reverses it, even mid-move. A door is shut while its ceiling sits on its floor.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_split: The floor goes down as the ceiling goes up. Closing, they meet: back where they were, or halfway for a door that started open.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_floor_lip: How far above the lowest neighbouring floor the floor stops.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_locked: Only an instigator with the required tag moves the door. Runs without an instigator entity (timers, On Start, ...) always move it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_pathfinde: A blocked Pathfinder with Opens Doors may open this door, as Doom's monsters do. Off keeps them out, like a door only the player can use.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_required_: The tag the instigator needs, e.g. one given by an Add Tag dispatch on a key pickup.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_locked_so: Played from the sector when an instigator without the tag tries the door. Empty: no sound.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.door_locked_me: Shown when an instigator without the tag tries the door. Empty: no message.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.light_speed: Light units (0-255) per second. 0 changes it instantly.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.sector_texture: The new floor and/or ceiling texture. It replaces every animation frame with this one, placed like the old first frame; the animation mode stays.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.change_tag: Adds or removes one of this object's own tags (the ones tag filters and Lua check), not a link tag.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.velocity: Added to, or replacing, the Rigidbody's velocity.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.move_relative: Position is an offset from where the entity is when this runs.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.component: Every component of this type on the entity.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.sprite_texture: Replaces all 8 textures of the entity's first Sprite, empty slots included. The sprite's direction mode is kept. Does nothing if the entity has no Sprite.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.world_position: Spawn at the position below instead of at this object plus an offset.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.sound: Played from this object's position; on the level itself it isn't positioned.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.relay: Runs every dispatch linked to this tag, after its own delay.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.reset_event: Sets the trigger count of every event linked to this tag back to 0.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.level: The level to switch to at the end of the frame. (Next Level) is the next one in Project Settings > Levels, and the first one after the last.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_ui_text: Replaces the text of this entity's first UI Text. Does nothing without one.
variables.tooltip.name: The variable's name. Conditions and dispatches keep working when it is renamed.
variables.tooltip.value: The value the variable starts with.
variables.tooltip.delete: Delete this variable. Conditions and dispatches that use it show it as missing; it reads as 0.
variables.notification.duplicate_name: A level or global variable with that name already exists.
settings.variables.title: Event Variables
settings.variables.tooltip: Numbers for event conditions that belong to this level. They go back to their starting values every time the level loads.
settings.level_events.title: Level Events
settings.level_events.tooltip: Events and dispatches that belong to the level itself, such as On Start and Timer.
settings.message.title: Message Box
settings.message.tooltip: How the text of Show Message dispatches looks in this level. Sizes are pixels at the project's UI Reference Height and scale with the window, like UI Text. The text colour is each dispatch's own.
settings.message.tooltip.font: A .ttf or .otf from the project. Empty uses the engine's font. Characters it lacks come from the engine's font.
settings.message.tooltip.font_size: Glyph size in pixels at the UI Reference Height.
settings.message.tooltip.anchor: The point of the screen the message (or the stack of messages) is placed against.
settings.message.tooltip.offset: Moves the message from the anchor. X goes right, Y goes down.
settings.message.tooltip.align: How lines of different widths line up inside the message.
settings.message.tooltip.wrap_width: Lines longer than this wrap between words. 0 never wraps; a new line in the text always starts one.
settings.message.tooltip.background: Draws a box behind each message.
settings.message.tooltip.background_colo: The box's colour and see-through-ness. With a texture, it tints the texture.
settings.message.tooltip.background_text: An image stretched over the box. Empty draws a solid box.
settings.message.tooltip.padding: Space between the text and the box's edges, left/right and top/bottom.
settings.message.tooltip.shadow: A copy of the text drawn behind it, moved by the offset.
settings.message.tooltip.shadow_offset: How far the shadow is moved. X goes right, Y goes down.
settings.message.tooltip.outline: A border drawn around the letters. Can be on together with the shadow.
settings.message.tooltip.fade: Seconds to fade in when shown and out before it goes, both inside the message's duration.
settings.message.tooltip.stack: Off: a new message replaces the one shown. On: messages stack, the newest at the top, and the others slide into place when one goes.
settings.message.tooltip.max_messages: With more than this many, the oldest goes at once.
editor.tooltip.project.variables: Numbers for event conditions shared by every level. They keep their value between levels and go back to their starting values when play starts.
editor.tooltip.inspector.name: This object's name, shown in the hierarchy.
editor.tooltip.entity.enabled: Unticked, the Entity is out of the game: its scripts stop (OnDisable fires), its sprites, models and UI are hidden, its colliders and Rigidbody stop (velocity is kept), rays pass through it, its flipbooks and sounds pause, and its events and dispatches don't run, except Enable and Destroy. Each component's own checkbox is left as it is.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_type: Down, Wait, Up: the floor goes down, waits, and comes back to where it started. Up, Wait, Down: the same, going up first. Perpetual: it keeps going between its low and high heights, waiting at each, until a Stop Movement on its floor; it heads first for the one further away.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_low_lip: Added to the lowest neighbouring floor. Negative goes below it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_high_lip: Added to the highest neighbouring floor. Negative stops below it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_wait: Seconds the lift waits at the far end (Perpetual: at each end).
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_collision: What the rising floor does when an entity is in the way. Retract takes it back down, waits and tries again. Going down never hits anything.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_retrigger: What happens when it runs again during a cycle. Go Again: heading back, it turns round; waiting, the wait starts over. Perpetual lifts ignore it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_start_sou: Played from the sector every time the floor starts moving. Empty: no sound.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_stop_soun: Played from the sector every time the floor stops. Empty: no sound.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.lift_locked: Only an instigator with the required tag moves the lift. Runs without an instigator entity (timers, On Start, ...) always move it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.stairs_step_he: This sector's floor rises by this much, the next step to this much above it, and so on. The next step is the one neighbouring sector with the same floor texture; the stairs end where there is none, or more than one.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.stairs_ignore_: Any single neighbouring sector is the next step, whatever its floor texture. Off: give the steps a floor texture the rooms around them don't use.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.light_effect_t: The light keeps changing between the sector's own light (as it was when the first effect started) and the dim light. Flicker: random bright and dim stretches, up to the times set. Strobe: bright, then dim, repeating. Glow: slides down to dim and back up at Speed. Fire Flicker: every Interval, a random step between bright and dim. None stops the effect and puts the sector's own light back. Set Light also stops it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.light_effect_d: The light it dims to: a colour, or the light of the darkest neighbouring sector when the effect starts.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.light_effect_s: On: every effect of this type with the same times runs on one clock, so their sectors change together. Off: each starts at a random point.
events.field.none_available: No fields Set Field can change.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_comp: Which of the entity's components to change. Only the types it has are listed.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_whic: Which component of that type, in the order the inspector lists them.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_fiel: The field to change. Scripts list their public fields of number, bool, text, vector, enum and texture types.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_oper: Set replaces the value. Add and Multiply work on each channel of a number, vector or colour. Toggle flips an on/off field.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_sour: Event Variable: every channel gets the variable's value; an on/off field is on when it isn't 0; text gets the number written out.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_over: Slides there instead of jumping. Only numbers, vectors and colours.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_spee: Units per second, per channel (colours are 0-1).
editor.tooltip.dispatches.set_field_reve: Puts back the value from before the first run, Revert After seconds after the change got there (sliding back at the same speed when Over Time is on). Running again while it waits restarts the wait and still goes back to that first value.
Seconds after the change got there.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.flow: What runs after this dispatch. Each step waits, checks its condition, then calls named dispatches. Steps run independently: stack several to branch or start several chains. Nothing follows if this dispatch didn't run (a disabled entity, a locked door).
editor.tooltip.dispatches.flow_wait: Seconds after this dispatch runs. 0 = the next frame.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.flow_condition: Checked once the wait is over, right before the call. Always, an event-variable comparison, or a random chance.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.flow_chance: Chance the step goes on, rolled each time.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.flow_add: Adds a step that calls one named dispatch after this one. The instigator stays the one that started the chain.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.name: What direct calls run this dispatch by. Several dispatches of one object can share a name: a call runs all of them.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.link_tag: The tag this dispatch listens on: every event with this tag runs it. (no tag): only direct calls run it.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.relay_mode: A Tag: runs every dispatch listening on the tag. A Named Dispatch: runs the dispatches with a name on one target, like an event's direct call.
events.call.hint.nothing_answers: Nothing tagged so has this name yet
events.call.hint.no_entity_answers: No entity in this level has this name yet
editor.tooltip.events.call_target: Whose dispatches this call runs. 'The entity that ...' is whoever caused the event, only known while playing: it runs that entity's own dispatches with the name, and entities without one ignore it.
editor.tooltip.events.call_object: Pick from the list, or drag one here from the hierarchy or the map.
editor.tooltip.events.call_tag: Every entity, sector and wall with this tag runs its dispatches with the name.
editor.tooltip.events.call_dispatch: Runs every dispatch with this name on the target. Renaming a dispatch doesn't update calls to it: re-pick the name.
editor.tooltip.events.call_add: Runs named dispatches of one target directly, besides (or instead of) the tag.
settings.music.title: Music
settings.music.tooltip: Sound files played one after another while the level runs, unpositioned. Lua's Music table and the Music dispatch control it.
settings.music.tooltip.add_track: Adds a track at the end. Drag a sound from the Asset Browser onto it.
settings.music.tooltip.remove: Removes this track from the list.
settings.music.tooltip.play_on_start: Starts the music when the level starts. Off: only Music.Start or a Music dispatch starts it. Music already playing the same list keeps playing when this level is loaded.
settings.music.tooltip.mode: Loop: the next track, back to the first after the last. Ping-pong: forward, then back (1, 2, 3, 2, 1...). Shuffle: every track once in a random order, then a new order. Once: the list once, then the music stops.
settings.music.tooltip.volume: 1 plays the files as they are, 0 is silent.
settings.music.tooltip.fade: Seconds the music fades out and the new track fades in when switching tracks, and fades out when stopped. 0 cuts straight away. A track ending on its own doesn't fade.
settings.music.tooltip.gap: Seconds of silence between a track ending and the next starting.
events.music.no_tracks: The level has no music. Add tracks in World Settings > Music.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.music_action: Controls the level's music (World Settings > Music). Play resumes a paused track, or starts the list from the first track.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.music_track: One of this level's music tracks. It plays now (fading if the level has a fade), and the list carries on from there.
editor.ui.text.tooltip.variable: Shows an event variable (level or global) instead of the text above, kept up to date while playing: Prefix + value + Suffix. Whole numbers show without decimals (42), others as short as they go (2.5). (none): the text above.
editor.ui.text.tooltip.prefix: Text before the value, e.g. "Ammo: ". Lua: UIText.prefix.
editor.ui.text.tooltip.suffix: Text after the value, e.g. " / 50". Lua: UIText.suffix.
editor.tooltip.dispatches.ui_text_part: Text: the UI Text's own text, shown when it shows no variable. Prefix / Suffix: the words around the variable it shows.
editor.tooltip.entity.persist_between_le: Ticked, Game.LoadLevel and the Load Level dispatch keep this entity: it goes on into the next level with its components, its running scripts (Lua state and Invokes), its sounds and its event trigger counts. Its scripts get OnLevelLoaded there, not Start.
editor.tooltip.entity.persistence_key: When the next level has an entity with the same key (its level copy), that entity is merged into this one and removed: components ticked Take Values from Level Copy (in their ... menu) take the copy's values, Transform by default, so the copy places it. Components only the copy has are added, and whatever pointed at the copy points at this entity.
editor.tooltip.entity.take_from_level_co: When this entity is carried into a level that has its level copy (same persistence key), this component takes the copy's values. A script restarts with the copy's field values. Unticked, it keeps its own.
editor.tooltip.ui.layout.editing: The level's own UI, or a UI layout: UI kept outside the levels, which each level can show (World Settings > UI Layouts). Only the one chosen here is shown.
editor.tooltip.ui.layout.new: Makes a new, empty UI layout in Assets/UI Layouts and opens it here.
editor.ui.layout.error_name: A name can't be empty, start or end with a dot, or hold \ / : * ? " < > |
editor.ui.layout.error_exists: There already is a UI layout with that name.
editor.tooltip.ui.layout.use_in_level: Shows this layout in the open level (World Settings > UI Layouts), on top of the layouts listed before it.
editor.tooltip.ui.layout.save: Saves this layout's file. Saving the level (Ctrl+S) saves every changed layout too.
editor.ui.layout.save_failed: Could not save the UI layout:
editor.tooltip.ui.layout.paste: Copies this layout's UI into the level's own UI, where it is in the layout. The copies aren't linked to the layout.
editor.ui.layout.pasted: Layout pasted into the level's UI
editor.ui.layout.links_hint: Events and fields here can only point at this layout's own entities.
settings.ui_layouts.title: UI Layouts
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip: The UI layouts this level shows, bottom first. The level's own UI is drawn on top of them all. A layout the next level shows too keeps going through Game.LoadLevel, with its state.
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip.add: Adds one of the project's UI layouts (.uilayout files) to this level.
settings.ui_layouts.none_left: No other UI layouts. Make one in the UI editor or the Asset Browser.
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip.edit: Opens the layout in the UI editor.
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip.layout: Which UI layout. Levels keep the layout by its ID, so renaming or moving the file doesn't break them.
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip.move_up: Draw it lower (under the one before it).
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip.move_down: Draw it higher (over the one after it).
settings.ui_layouts.tooltip.remove: Stop showing this layout in this level.
